prompt: Name a song on the original 1991 release of Nirvana's Nevermind.
label: Final Dig
valueLogic: The four singles come first. Polly and Something in the Way follow, both being distinctive. The deep album tracks are the tail - Lounge Act, Stay Away and On a Plain are the three that even people who love the record struggle to produce.
note: Endless, Nameless is a non-busting distractor: it's a hidden track on later pressings, not on the printed twelve, and the first pressings didn't have it at all.

answers.name: Smells Like Teen Spirit
answers.fact: Track one. The title came from a deodorant brand, which Cobain did not know at the time.

answers.name: Come as You Are
answers.fact: Track three, and the second single.

answers.name: Lithium
answers.fact: Track five, and the third single.

answers.name: In Bloom
answers.fact: Track two, and the fourth single, with the video shot as a 1960s variety show.

answers.name: Polly
answers.fact: Track six, and one of the record's two quiet acoustic songs.

answers.name: Something in the Way
answers.fact: Track twelve, and the closer. Recorded almost in a whisper.

answers.name: Drain You
answers.fact: Track eight, and a song Cobain said he rated as highly as Teen Spirit.

answers.name: Territorial Pissings
answers.fact: Track seven, and the most abrasive thing on the record.

answers.name: Stay Away
answers.fact: Track ten, originally titled Pay to Play.

answers.name: Lounge Act
answers.fact: Track nine, and the hardest of the twelve to name.

distractors.name: Endless, Nameless
distractors.note: A hidden track after a long silence on most pressings, and not on the printed twelve-track listing.

distractors.name: Heart-Shaped Box
distractors.note: From In Utero, two years later.

distractors.name: Where Did You Sleep Last Night
The Man Who Sold the World
Aneurysm
distractors.note: A B-side from the same era, not on the album.

distractors.name: Sliver
distractors.note: A 1990 single, not on the album.
